data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts following an explicit checklist will produce more reliable judgments than a single expert for verifiable tasks because the checklist eliminates 'premature closure' and cognitive tunneling.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task complexity exceeds the checklist's coverage (checklist is 'lossy compression', per SRC_003)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist contains contradictory items that the non-experts lack the domain knowledge to resolve (SCR_002)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'trained' non-experts suffer from groupthink that overrides the checklist's individual checkpoints (SCR_012)","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a cognitive forcing function that mandates a breadth-first search of the problem space. While an expert's intuition is a high-speed heuristic that prioritizes the most likely cause (leading to 'premature closure' as noted in SCR_008), the checklist ensures that low-probability but high-impact variables are explicitly checked, effectively raising the floor of reliability by preventing catastrophic omissions of basic requirements.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
